evidence: coop/crates/coop-launcher/src/session.rs:103-119 promotes realtime and heartbeat after a control burst, but realtime remains ordered before heartbeat in the service-first branch and both remain behind control in the normal branch.

coop/crates/coop-launcher/src/session.rs:2323-2349 resets control_burst to zero whenever a realtime event is consumed, so simultaneous continuously-ready control and realtime streams can repeat eight control events plus one realtime event forever without selecting an already-due heartbeat.

coop/crates/coop-launcher/src/session.rs:153-170 and 2729-2734 have the analogous cutover ordering: a continuously-ready realtime event wins ahead of Activate after every control burst, resets the burst, and can prevent Ready activation until the bounded lifecycle buffer fails closed.

coop/crates/coop-launcher/src/session.rs:4948-4958 deliberately waits for a heartbeat before the WebSocket server begins sending lifecycle frames, while the terminal fairness test at 5091-5171 closes the realtime peer before flooding PlayerState; neither test makes control, realtime, and heartbeat/activation ready together.
findings.impact: An authenticated high-rate local state stream combined with a server lifecycle stream can starve lease heartbeat indefinitely, causing avoidable lease expiry while the WebSocket remains active. The same arbitration can prevent a valid Ready cutover and turn otherwise processable bounded traffic into terminal failure, so F-830116ED is not fully resolved.
findings.observation: The r2 burst limiter bounds consecutive control selections but does not provide round-robin or deadline priority across realtime and heartbeat/activation; consuming realtime resets the only fairness counter.
findings.recommendation: Track service debt independently for heartbeat, realtime, and Ready activation, or check due heartbeat/activation before resetting the control budget. Guarantee each continuously-ready service branch runs within a fixed number of other selections. Add deterministic tests with simultaneous sustained PlayerState and lifecycle readiness that prove a due heartbeat occurs and Ready activation completes without buffer failure.

evidence: coop/crates/coop-launcher/src/session.rs:4836-4998 now covers pending-mint freshest-state handoff and a successful joined lifecycle, and 5000-5088 covers active reset teardown.

No activation-level test in coop/crates/coop-launcher/src/session.rs induces ControlTerminalCause::LifecycleOverflow or InteractionOverflow after activation, and no successful active coordinator test drives MgbaExited or SidecarExited through the session cleanup branch at 2303-2319.

The sealed LRA2-006 criterion requires lifecycle mapping/backpressure, cleanup ordering, and task termination coverage; direct pump/core tests do not prove their composition through run_until_shutdown_with_realtime.
findings.impact: F-F3308A85 is only partially resolved: freshest-state and reset evidence now exist, but active queue-backpressure and child-failure composition can regress without a failing activation-level test.
findings.observation: The r2 suite closes most of the earlier integration gap but still omits two explicitly required active terminal paths through the production lifecycle.
findings.recommendation: Add deterministic activation tests that saturate the lifecycle or interaction lane and that exit each supervised child after Ready. Assert one attempt, no post-terminal ROM output, disabled lifecycle, coordinator join before raw settlement, pump/peer reaping, and retained cleanup evidence on failure.
